clue.text: Poor writer introduces old sayings — they have a cutting edge

parts.note: a hack is a writer of poor, routine work
saws are old proverbs or maxims

explanation.surface: A second-rate author pads his work with proverbs, though they are pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' is just a link here: the poor writer comes first and the sayings follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacksaws are tools whose toothed blades cut metal, so each has a cutting edge.

clue.text: Coiffure for a show followed by a party

parts.note: Hair is a famous rock musical
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone gets their hair styled for a show and the party afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' puts the party after the show; Hair is the 1960s musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a style in which hair is cut and arranged, the same as a coiffure.

clue.text: Foul-sounding companion breaking into the money

definitions.note: the definition means something that sounds like 'foul', a fowl, i.e. a breed of chicken

indicators.note: breaking into means the companion gets inside the money

parts.note: coin is money
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A nasty-sounding companion bursts into the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul-sounding' defines by homophone: it is a fowl, the Cochin breed of chicken. 'breaking into' signals the container; the companion is a Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochin is a large breed of domestic poultry, so a bird whose description sounds like 'foul'.

clue.text: Material store in the borders of Egypt

parts.note: stock is a store or supply

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cloth stockpiled at the edges of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the borders of' takes the first and last letters of Egypt, E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockinet is a soft elastic knitted fabric, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Six-foot swimmer abused me at a town bar

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tall complains of being insulted at a pub in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-foot' looks like a tall person but means six-legged: the insect has six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A water boatman is an aquatic insect, with six legs, that rows through ponds on its back.

clue.text: Mulled wine provided for a man on board

definitions.meaning: a hot spiced drink of port or wine with oranges goes by the name of a churchman
a chess piece that moves diagonally on the board

explanation.walkthrough: The held text wrongly repeats the 1 Across clue in front; the page prints only 'Mulled wine provided for a man on board'. 'provided for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece and an old English spiced mulled drink both share the name of a senior cleric.

clue.text: Bury prisoner not born in france

indicators.note: not means the French word is taken away from the prisoner

parts.note: an internee is a person confined, especially in wartime
nee is French for born (feminine)

explanation.surface: Locking away a captive who was not born in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'born in France' is French: NEE (as in a woman's maiden name). Removing it from INTERNEE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a corpse in a grave, the same as to bury it.

clue.text: Leading women providing horse with quarters

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Female leads supply a horse with stabling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin; 'quarters' gives two compass points, E and S. 'providing' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroines are the female leads or principal women characters in a story.

clue.text: Be inquisitive about work she contrived to foretell

indicators.note: about places the nosy verb around the other pieces

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy
op (opus) is a work

indicators.note: contrived means the three letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Snooping into a woman's job as she schemes to predict the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges 'she' to HES; 'about' then wraps the nosy verb round the work plus those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To prophesy is to predict what will happen in the future.

clue.text: Popular talk about Old English — only just begun

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the talk and the language are moved around

parts.note: chat is informal talk

explanation.surface: A popular discussion of Anglo-Saxon has barely got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container but is the anagram signal, making CHOATE from the talk and the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate describes something rudimentary, at the earliest stage of development.

clue.text: The sound, perhaps, of Orestes prematurely coming to grief

indicators.note: coming to grief means falling apart, so the remaining letters are rearranged
prematurely means the name is stopped before its final letter

explanation.surface: A story of the Greek hero Orestes meeting an untimely tragic end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prematurely' cuts the last S from Orestes, leaving ORESTE; 'coming to grief' then rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo is a kind of two-channel reproduced sound, so sound of that kind is an example.

clue.text: Not in the groove — and that's confidential

definitions.meaning: literally, a needle that has left the track of a gramophone disc
said of remarks not meant for publication

explanation.walkthrough: 'groove' looks like the idiom 'in the groove' (performing well) but means the spiral track on a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the record means unofficial and not to be quoted, while literally it describes a stylus away from a disc.

clue.text: GP in a thousand — cordial too!

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A doctor among a thousand patients is also warm and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like an adjective (friendly) but is the noun: a sweet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweetened fruit beverage, one sort of thing you can have to sup.

clue.text: Brighten up advert, say, by mistake

indicators.note: say signals that the verb is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it
bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone livens up an advertisement by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advert' is the verb meaning refer, not an advertisement; 'say' turns REFER into the sound-alike REFUR. BISH is old British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurbish is to renovate or smarten something so it looks fresh again.

clue.text: Ineligibility for inclusion in Fuller's book

definitions.text: Ineligibility for inclusion in Fuller's book

parts.words: Ineligibility for inclusion in Fuller's book
parts.note: Thomas Fuller wrote The History of the Worthies of England; someone not good enough to appear in it would lack the quality of a worthy

explanation.walkthrough: Fuller's book is Thomas Fuller's 17th-century 'Worthies of England'; failing to qualify for it is being not worthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of not deserving merit or esteem, here pictured as failing to qualify for a book of eminent people.

clue.text: Rashness shown by a trendy, amusing person

parts.note: in means fashionable
a caution is a funny or remarkable person

explanation.surface: Recklessness displayed by a fashionable joker.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'caution' is old slang for an amusing or startling person. 'shown by a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Incaution is a lack of care, the same as recklessness.

clue.text: Glass seen around church? Rather!

indicators.note: around places the word for rather around the church

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in 'I'd sooner'

explanation.surface: A stained glass window seen round a church, and what a sight!
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; the surface's exclamation 'Rather!' is really the word meaning 'preferably'. A schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a large drinking vessel for sherry or beer.

clue.text: Story told before City function is held

indicators.note: is held means the city and function letters are held inside the word for before

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
EC is the postal district for the City of London
a do is a social function

explanation.surface: A tale recounted ahead of a City event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is held' signals the container. The City is the City of London, whose postcode letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing account of an incident.

clue.text: Nicest county represented in Parliament?

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether the loveliest shire has its own member at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' does double duty in the surface: the rearrangement signal, and the sense of a district that sends a member to the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency is an electoral district whose voters elect a Member of Parliament.

clue.text: In Utah it identifies an island

indicators.note: In means the island sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A claim that something in Utah points to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Utah is a US state, misleading because the island is in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Crime makes youth leader sore at first

indicators.note: at first puts the sore before the letter

parts.note: a felon is an old word for a whitlow, an inflamed sore on a finger

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A young gang leader's crime causes upset at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore' is a noun: a felon is an old word for an abscess on a finger. 'at first' puts it before Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious offence in law.

clue.text: Swing to and fro in the current manner

definitions.text: Swing to and fro in the current manner

parts.words: Swing to and fro in the current manner
parts.note: alternating electric current reverses direction back and forth, just like a pendulum moving each way

explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but means electric current, whose alternating flow swings back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move back and forth regularly, as alternating electricity does.

clue.text: Be prone to embrace students in the north of France?

definitions.note: a definition by example: a place found in northern France

indicators.note: to embrace means the lying word surrounds the students

parts.note: to lie is to be prone
L is a learner, so LL are students

explanation.surface: Lying down to hug students up in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' signals the container; students are learners, L as on British learner-driver plates. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city near the Belgian border, an example of somewhere in that region.

clue.text: Employment of wise man by university

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A job for a wise man at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link placing the sage beside U.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the use or handling of something, so employment of a thing in that sense.

clue.text: Accountant abandons pet ? The idiot!

indicators.note: abandons means the accountant's letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: to pet is to kiss and cuddle, or canoodle
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant leaves his dog behind, the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but is the verb to cuddle, CANOODLE; dropping CA leaves the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an old informal word for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Crafty circular from a representative of the people

parts.note: politic can mean shrewd or cunning
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cunning leaflet sent out by an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular' looks like a leaflet but just gives the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is an informal word for a politician, someone elected to stand for voters.

clue.text: Jacket for Hornblower at the start of his career

definitions.meaning: a short, double-breasted thick coat worn by sailors

definitions.text: Hornblower at the start of his career
definitions.meaning: C. S. Forester's hero Horatio Hornblower began as a midshipman, nicknamed in naval slang after the sails he reefed

explanation.walkthrough: Hornblower is C. S. Forester's fictional naval officer, who starts as a midshipman; midshipmen were called reefers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a navy-style double-breasted coat and a junior officer in old naval slang.

clue.text: Sort of parade of fish and bird in New York

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A procession in New York featuring fish and birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. An identity parade is the British term for a police line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity parade is a police line-up of suspects, so the word describes one type of such a lineup.
